facts.fact: Ad inventory is the advertising space a publisher has available to sell.
facts.quote: is the advertising space a publisher has available to sell

facts.fact: CPM is the cost per 1,000 impressions on a given inventory.
facts.quote: Cost per 1,000 impressions on that inventory

facts.fact: An impression is one delivery of an ad into a slot.
facts.quote: One delivery of an ad into a slot

facts.fact: Fill rate is the share of available ad slots that sold.
facts.quote: Share of available slots that sold

facts.fact: On a streaming app, a 30-second mid-roll slot inside a comedy pod is an example of inventory.
facts.quote: a 30-second mid-roll slot inside a comedy pod is inventory

facts.fact: Seasonality such as Q4 often tightens ad inventory and lifts prices.
facts.quote: Seasonality (for example, Q4) often tightens inventory and lifts prices.

facts.fact: Remnant inventory is capacity that did not sell in a direct or reserved deal and is often sold through automated auctions at lower prices.
facts.quote: Capacity that did not sell in a direct or reserved deal. Often sold through automated auctions at lower prices.

facts.fact: The glossary page was published on 2026-09-17.
Adwave lets advertisers set a daily budget starting from $30/day, and the system buys across the channel mix without the advertiser managing publisher deals.
facts.quote: set location and a daily budget (from **$30/day**), and the system buys across the mix without you managing publisher deals

facts.fact: In the page's illustrative example, a stream of inventory clearing at a $25 CPM means $250 buys about 10,000 impressions.
facts.quote: if a stream of inventory clears at a **$25** CPM, **$250** buys about **10,000** impressions

facts.fact: In the page's illustrative example, if targeting leaves only 4,000 matching impressions available that day, delivery slows and effective cost can rise.
facts.quote: If targeting is so tight that only 4,000 matching impressions exist that day, the system cannot invent slots.
